script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 29. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Oil formed over 300 million years from ancient organisms.  We're burning through centuries of accumulation every few minutes.  When it's gone, it's gone—at least for another few hundred million years.

Non-renewable doesn't mean never—it means not on relevant timescales. Oil will form again, but not for millions of years. For practical purposes, once depleted, it's gone. Non-renewables follow depletion curves.  Easy deposits get used first.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Some things don't come back.  Recognize what's finite and treat it accordingly.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Finite Resource Audit - What Won't Come Back?.

Here's your activity: What in your life is truly non-renewable—time, specific opportunities, irreplaceable relationships, unique moments? How are you spending these finite resources? Are you using them for worthy purposes or wasting them on trivial things? This helps you identify non-renewable resources and use them wisely.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about things that run out can be applied to finite resource audit - what won't come back?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
